reviewMethod.methodNotesMd: Reviewed the Contract StructureDefinition report, the Contract resource-review context, R4/R6 Contract StructureDefinitions, and the deterministic aggregate only after forming the resource-level judgment. No direct Contract behavior findings were present. Shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings were considered as context only because the assigned resource is `Contract`, not `Resource` or `DomainResource`.

r4Maturity.effectMd: R4 Contract was FMM 1/trial-use, so a hard break does not carry the same presumption against change as mature or normative content. The legal/agreement domain is still business and audit relevant, so real lossy migrations matter, but low maturity makes isolated remodels easier to accept when they solve a coherent modeling problem.

overall.oneLineConclusion: Contract keeps its R4 resource identity and overall shape; only the action-reason remodel is a hard local R4-to-R6 instance break.

reasoning.thesisMd: `Contract` is not a resource whose R6 migration is already dominated by resource replacement or broad redesign. The resource remains the same DomainResource specialization at the same canonical URL, with no local cardinality strengthening, modifier-flag strengthening, new local invariant burden, required binding code removal, or direct operation/search/HTTP behavior finding. The important compatibility issue is concentrated in `Contract.term.action.reason` and its removed R4 sibling fields.
reasoning.migrationShapeMd: The actual migration shape is a mostly stable resource plus one targeted structural transform. R4 had separate `term.action.reason` strings, `reasonCode` CodeableConcepts, and `reasonReference` References; R6 consolidates these into repeating `CodeableReference` at `term.action.reason`. Contract instances that do not use those fields may need little more than regenerated models and ordinary R4-to-R6 validation checks, while instances that do use them need explicit mapping policy.
reasoning.compatibilityLeverageMd: Because a whole-resource migration program is not already unavoidable, avoidable local breaks still retain normal per-change leverage. Even for implementers that must transform action reasons, that local chore does not justify ignoring other low-cost compatibility preservation opportunities; however, the other Contract findings are either reverse-only, same-wire-shape, semantic, or example-binding concerns rather than additional hard R4-to-R6 instance breaks.
reasoning.lessBreakingAlternativesMd: The main less-breaking alternative would have retained the R4 reason, reasonCode, and reasonReference elements as deprecated fields while adding a new CodeableReference element. That would preserve more R4 payloads but would also duplicate rationale representations and require conflict/precedence rules. Given Contract's FMM 1 status and CodeableReference's coherent resolution of parallel arrays, this is not a clear low-cost preservation win. The publicationDate wording could be clarified with additive lifecycle guidance, but it is not a syntactic break and R4 already contained update-date language.
reasoning.behaviorImpactMd: There are no direct Contract behavior findings in the supplied context. The shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings, including Resource-level operation removals and special search-parameter metadata changes, can affect generic infrastructure around Contract but are not Contract-specific evidence of a resource-level Contract migration program.
reasoning.comparisonToDeterministicAggregateMd: The deterministic aggregate reached the same high-level outcome: `majorMigrationAlreadyUnavoidable = No`, `mostly-stable-with-local-breaks`, and `preserve-compatibility-per-change`. My independent review agrees with that posture but treats the action-reason change as a substantive targeted remodel rather than just a counted hard break; it still remains too localized to make major Contract migration unavoidable.
reasoning.uncertaintyMd: Confidence is high for the structural conclusion because the R4 and R6 StructureDefinitions are directly comparable. Confidence is lower for real-world prevalence and terminology implications because official change rationale, narrative pages, production adoption evidence, and authoritative terminology expansions were not part of the local evidence.

findingConsiderations.title: Contract.term.action reason fields were merged and retyped to CodeableReference
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is the only clear hard local instance break. R4 primitive strings and the sibling `reasonCode`/`reasonReference` arrays do not validate as the R6 CodeableReference shape without transformation, and R6 items containing both concept and reference are not losslessly representable in the separate R4 arrays. It drives the need for targeted migration logic, but not for a whole-resource Contract migration program.

findingConsiderations.title: Contract.contentDefinition.publicationDate now describes last significant change rather than publication
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This matters for legal/audit semantics because an original publication date could be misread as a last-significant-change date. It is still local and non-syntactic: the path, type, and cardinality remain optional dateTime, and the R4 definition already said the date must change for version, status, and substantive content changes.

findingConsiderations.title: Contract.term.text changed from string to markdown
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The FHIR primitive type code changes, so generated models and renderers may need updates, especially around markdown sanitization. The wire representation remains a JSON string and ordinary R4 text values are not made invalid, so this is not resource-level migration evidence.

findingConsiderations.title: Contract.author can now reference RelatedPerson
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This widens the R6 target set while preserving all R4 targets. It can complicate R6-to-R4 conversion or exhaustive generated type checks when R6 data actually uses RelatedPerson, but it does not create an R4-to-R6 instance break.

findingConsiderations.title: Contract.term.action performer example bindings changed
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The performer value set recommendations changed, but the bindings remain example strength and the affected elements remain CodeableConcept. This should be treated as a local UI/profile/terminology-review chore rather than a base R4-to-R6 validation break.

findingConsiderations.title: Resource $meta-add is removed from R6 core
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is a real shared Resource-level behavior concern for generic metadata clients, but it is not a Contract-specific operation or search surface finding. It should not be counted as evidence that Contract itself has been remodeled.

findingConsiderations.title: Core special/profile search parameters changed type metadata for _content, _text, _query, and _profile
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The shared search-parameter metadata change can affect generic clients that search across resource types including Contract, but the review rules treat shared Resource/DomainResource behavior as context only for a concrete resource such as Contract.

recommendedNextActions.actionMd: Define and test the targeted `term.action.reason` migration: map R4 `reason` strings to R6 `CodeableReference.concept.text`, map `reasonCode` to `concept`, map `reasonReference` to `reference`, and flag R6 concept+reference pairs when converting back to R4.

Audit any Contract lifecycle workflows that used `contentDefinition.publicationDate`; preserve original-publication semantics separately when the R4 value was not maintained as a last-significant-change date.

Regenerate Contract models and UI/terminology helpers for the markdown type, RelatedPerson author target, and changed example bindings; these are local implementation chores rather than standards-level blockers.

caveats: No official Contract R4-to-R6 change rationale or Jira history was reviewed; design motivation is inferred from the computable artifacts.
Terminology value set expansions were not performed, so example-binding operational impact may be understated for local profiles that strengthened those bindings.
Shared Resource and DomainResource behavior findings are intentionally not scored as Contract-specific findings.
